tagline: Two old roads out of Monticello, through pine and pasture.
intro: Two state highways, SR 11 and SR 83, fan out north from Monticello, and between them they make 29 miles of Jasper County pine forest and rolling pasture to the county line.

They are old roads. Native Americans and Methodist circuit riders used them, and Highway 83 was part of the Seven Island Stage Coach Road, which ran from Augusta to New Orleans and the Natchez Trace. Monticello itself was founded in 1808 as the new county's seat and named for Thomas Jefferson's estate.

moments.title: Charlie Elliott Wildlife Center
moments.text: Near Mansfield the state manages 6,400 acres of forest, lakes and fields, with 22 public fishing lakes and ponds and a short hiking trail named for Murder Creek.

moments.title: Jasper County Courthouse
moments.text: Monticello's courthouse of 1907, the county's third, stood in for the courthouse in the exterior shots of My Cousin Vinny.

moments.title: Shady Dale
moments.text: Out SR 83, where it meets SR 142, a town founded about 1880 on the site of a Creek settlement took a name that simply described the place.
